exercise.name: Resistance Band Standing Hip Abduction

reference.title: Resistance Band Standing Hip Abduction
reference.listing: Catalog entry only (gymvisual.com not read; blocked by the proxy). Movement from the exercise name and standard coaching.

equipment: Resistance band (mini loop around the ankles)

breathing.pattern: Exhale as the leg moves out, inhale as it returns.
breathing.cadence: About 1.2 s out, 0.5 s hold, 1.8 s back

prescription.progression: Stronger band, or move the band from above the knees to the ankles

cues.text: Loop the band around both ankles, stand tall on the left leg and put the hands on the hips.
Breathe out and push the straight right leg out to the side, toes forward.
Pause at about 30 degrees with the pelvis level.
Breathe in and let the band draw the leg back slowly.
Keep a little tension before the feet meet; repeat, then switch legs.

mistakes.fix: Stay tall; the hips do the work, not a side bend.
Keep the toes forward so the hip does not rotate out.
Control the return; slower back than out.
Keep the pelvis level; make the arc smaller if it tips.

kinematics.norm: About 25-35 degrees against a band (clinical opinion); standing abduction excites the gluteus medius well (Distefano 2009; Boren 2011)
Mini loop around both ankles; tension grows as the feet separate (elastic resistance, Andersen 2010)

sources.title: GymVisual #14470, Resistance Band Standing Hip Abduction, video (movement reference)
Distefano et al. 2009, gluteal muscle activation during common therapeutic exercises (J Orthop Sports Phys Ther 39(7):532-540)
Boren et al. 2011, EMG analysis of gluteus medius and gluteus maximus during rehabilitation exercises (Int J Sports Phys Ther 6(3):206-223; PMC3201064)

Andersen, Andersen, Mortensen, Poulsen, Bjørnlund and Zebis 2010, muscle activation and perceived loading during rehabilitation exercises: comparison of dumbbells and elastic resistance (Phys Ther 90(4):538-549)

cautions: Stop if sharp pain, numbness or cramping occurs.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
Check the band for nicks before use; a snapping band can sting.
modify: Poor balance: hold a wall with one hand.
Hip pinching: make the arc smaller.

muscleNotes.glute_med_r: Prime mover of hip abduction; standing and side-lying abduction rank high for gluteus medius (Distefano 2009; Boren 2011).
muscleNotes.glute_med_l: Holds the pelvis level over the stance leg, also working against the band (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.obliques_l: Resists leaning away from the band (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.calves_l: Balance on the stance foot (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.adductors_r: Lengthen as the leg moves out (clinical opinion).

guides.label: Leg sweeps out to the side
